justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I inferred to be a current price level near $291–$292, which likely represents a broad equity index or similar financial instrument trading in that range. For the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing price with minimal drift, assuming mean-reverting intraday dynamics and no major scheduled catalysts to force a large directional move. At one week, I allowed for slightly more positive drift, consistent with a mild bullish baseline assumption — perhaps reflecting an environment where monetary policy expectations are relatively stable and no immediate shock is priced in. At one month, I extended that drift further, incorporating a longer-run tendency for equity prices to drift upward over time, though the increment remains modest given the uncertainty that compounds over that horizon.

The confidence interval widths reflect the well-known scaling of uncertainty with time. At one day, the 90% CI spans roughly 15 points, consistent with typical daily realized volatility for a broad index at this price level — approximately 1–2% on either side. At one week, the interval widens to 30 points total, reflecting roughly the square-root-of-time scaling of volatility as well as the accumulation of news, economic data releases, and sentiment shifts across five trading sessions. By one month, the interval opens to 58 points, acknowledging that a full month can encompass multiple macro data prints, central bank communications, geopolitical developments, and earnings surprises that compound directional uncertainty substantially.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes well outside my stated intervals. On the downside, a sharper-than-expected deterioration in economic data — such as a surprise spike in unemployment, a credit event, or an escalation in geopolitical tensions — could produce a move far below my lower bounds. A sudden liquidity crunch or a policy mistake by a major central bank could also trigger outsized selling. On the upside, an unexpectedly strong macro print, a dovish pivot signal, or a resolution of an existing geopolitical risk could fuel a rally that exceeds my upper bounds at the one-week or one-month horizon. My intervals are calibrated around a base case of roughly normal market functioning, so any tail event — financial, geopolitical, or otherwise — represents a genuine risk of exceeding these bounds.

It is also worth acknowledging the epistemic uncertainty in my forecast itself. I do not have real-time market data, so my starting price anchor is inferred rather than observed, which introduces an additional layer of uncertainty that is not fully captured in my stated intervals. If the true current price differs meaningfully from my assumption, all three point estimates would shift accordingly, and the intervals would need to be re-centered.
